fig_equity_time.webp.caption: Share of each year's single-country studies about low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): 17% in 2010 → 35% in 2025, against the 83% of global disease burden (GBD 2023 all-cause DALYs) those countries carry (dashed line). Studies naming a single country with a known income group (26,126); 2026 is partial and left out. Income group: the World Bank classification in force on 1 January of the publication year (World Bank historical classifications). For 2026 publications only, missing FY2026 classifications use FY2025 low income for Ethiopia and FY2021 upper-middle income for Venezuela (FY2025 also unavailable); these are analysis exceptions.

fig_metric.webp.caption: Share of eligible studies reporting each comparable metric. The metric flips with income: high-income research reports QALYs (54%) and almost no DALYs (1%); low-income research does the reverse (39% DALYs, 8% QALYs) — so rich and poor settings are measured in different units. Base: 41,657 eligible studies (income shown for single-country studies, by the World Bank group in force on 1 January of the publication year); a study may report neither, one, or both. For 2026 publications only, missing FY2026 classifications use FY2025 low income for Ethiopia and FY2021 upper-middle income for Venezuela (FY2025 also unavailable); these are analysis exceptions.

fig_intervention_mix.webp.caption: Share of each income group's eligible single-country studies whose primary intervention class is the given type (the optional secondary class is not folded in). Pharmaceuticals peak in upper-middle-income settings (46.6%) and fall to 17.9% at low income, where they stay narrowly ahead of care-model and organisational studies (17.3%); vaccines rise steadily with lower income (4.7% → 13.8%) while surgery (13.8% → 7.7%) and devices (8.5% → 3.0%) fall. Base: 27,930 eligible single-country studies with a World Bank income group in force on 1 January of the publication year. Intervention classes were assigned by a large language model from each abstract (one pass), checked against a keyword list, the topic clusters and a second model; they have not been checked by people. For 2026 publications only, missing FY2026 classifications use FY2025 low income for Ethiopia and FY2021 upper-middle income for Venezuela (FY2025 also unavailable); these are analysis exceptions.

paper05.webp.caption: Percentage of each income group's disease-coded studies that name each disease area, across the 14 harmonised groups (maternal & neonatal includes the MeSH pregnancy-complications branch C12.050.703; mental & substance use is MeSH F03). Rows run from areas most concentrated in low-income research (top) to high-income research (bottom): infectious disease dominates lower-income groups (79% of low-income and 61% of lower-middle-income studies), neoplasms and cardiovascular disease the high-income group. A study naming several areas appears in each, so columns sum above 100%. Income group: the World Bank classification in force on 1 January of the publication year. For 2026 publications only, missing FY2026 classifications use FY2025 low income for Ethiopia and FY2021 upper-middle income for Venezuela (FY2025 also unavailable); these are analysis exceptions.

fig_theme_rank.webp.caption: The 15 most-LMIC and 15 most-high-income of 73 research topics (found by clustering title-and-abstract embeddings) (all themes: 28%  LMIC). The high-income panel is shown first, plotted as each theme's high-income share (dementia leads at 93%); the LMIC panel as its LMIC share (malaria and dengue leads at 86%): 36%–86% LMIC vs 7%–16% LMIC. n per theme = single-country studies with a World Bank income group in force on 1 January of the publication year. For 2026 publications only, missing FY2026 classifications use FY2025 low income for Ethiopia and FY2021 upper-middle income for Venezuela (FY2025 also unavailable); these are analysis exceptions.

fig_inequality.webp.title: Research concentration within lower-income countries
fig_inequality.webp.caption: Base: 106 LMIC countries with GBD 2023 all-cause DALYs; 8,732 study–country pairs; 2 countries have no study. Countries ordered by studies per DALY. The first 41 countries crossing 50% of burden carry 53.9% of burden and 1,455 pairs (16.7%); the marker is at these actual coordinates. The five countries with the greatest burden (India, China, Nigeria, Indonesia, Pakistan) instead carry 51.7% of burden and 48.1% of evidence. Gini = 0.49. Country grouping uses July 2026 income classifications; studies span 2010–2026, final year partial. Each multi-country study counts once per country.

fig_reach_time.webp.title: How country coverage changes over time
fig_reach_time.webp.caption: Cumulative reach through each publication year. Countries are grouped by the World Bank classification in force on 1 January of that year; the denominator excludes unavailable country-year groups. Taiwan uses the recorded high-income override. A country is reached once any eligible study has named it by that year, including studies from its earlier income groups. In 2025, solid lines cover 154 classified countries from the 155-country website list (2 unreached); dashed lines cover 197 classified/overridden Natural Earth Sovereign country/Country entities (21 unreached), with no population floor. Denominators vary by year; 197 is not a fixed count of all World Bank economies. 2026 is partial and omitted, so the Ethiopia/Venezuela 2026 fallback does not affect these lines.

fig_deficit.webp.title: Where research counts differ most from burden shares
fig_deficit.webp.caption: Base: all 204 national GBD 2023 locations, including zero-study locations; 31,627 unique study–country pairs. Expected studies = this pair total × the country's share of DALYs across the same 204 locations. Hong Kong, Cayman Islands, French Guiana and Guadeloupe have no row in the national GBD export and their pairs are excluded. Bars show the 16 largest deficits and 8 largest surpluses. This larger country set differs from the 154-country website burden analysis (31,471 pairs). Country colours use July 2026 income groups. Studies published 2010–2026, final year partial; GBD 2023 all-cause DALYs. Proportionality is a reference point.
